title: Morphogenetic pattern memory habituates: repeatedly amputated axolotl limbs stop regrowing

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Morphogenetic pattern memory habituates: repeatedly amputated axolotl limbs stop regrowing

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The anatomical setpoint that guides regeneration is a pattern memory that is stable but modifiable by experience; for example, repeated amputation of axolotl limbs leads the tissue to habituate to the loss and eventually stop trying to regrow.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Memory and target morphology

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This pattern memory can, like any good memory, be modified by experience (it is stable, but also labile to the right kinds of stimuli). For example, repeated amputation of axolotl limbs leads to the tissue habituating to the loss of limb and eventually giving up trying to re-grow (Bryant et al. 2017).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Memory and target morphology”. Scope: Axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) limb regeneration and regenerating animals generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decline in regeneration across repeated amputations is a clear longitudinal outcome. Existing observations can test that pattern, but distinguishing memory-like habituation from cumulative tissue damage requires data and controls that may not exist publicly.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use limb-level longitudinal records across serial amputations to model regeneration probability, time, and completeness by amputation number, controlling for age, location, scarring, and health. A progressive failure specific to repeated history supports habituation operationally, while tissue exhaustion remains a rival.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw serial-amputation records may not be public.

Pattern memory is an interpretation, not a direct measurement.

Scarring, senescence, and stem-cell depletion can mimic habituation.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Repeated-amputation outcomes and a matching expression series are public enough to test whether regeneration declines and whether the decline looks like a wound-healing program. That can confirm the empirical stop and can favour a rival to pattern-memory habituation. It does not measure a stored anatomical setpoint being edited by experience, and it covers axolotl forelimbs rather than regenerating animals generally.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count axolotl forelimbs that reach digits after one through five amputations in the same plane, and contrast gene expression in limbs that have stopped with first-amputation controls. A progressive drop in completed regenerates would support the empirical decline, and no drop would refute it; expression dominated by a persistent wound-healing or amphiregulin response would favour scarring over habituation of an anatomical setpoint.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fibrosis and elevated amphiregulin, the study's own mechanism, mimic giving up on a target morphology.

The success-versus-amputation curve is in the paper's figures; the expression series is only the failed-versus-control contrast at one stage.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.45
data existence: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.72
